content: Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of allergic rhinitis and symptoms of the common cold. It is commonly associated with side effects such as diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and drowsiness. Adult Dosage and Indications: 1. FDA-Approved Dosage: For 4-hour allergy tablets: Take 1 tablet (4 mg) every 4 to 6 hours, with a maximum of 6 tablets in 24 hours. For 8-hour allergy tablets: Take 1 tablet (8 mg) every 8 to 12 hours, with a maximum of 3 tablets in 24 hours. For 12-hour tablets: Take 1 tablet (12 mg) every 12 hours, with a maximum of 2 tablets in 24 hours. For prevention of allergic rhinitis symptoms, start with 4 mg (syrup or plain tablet) three times daily and increase every three days as tolerated, up to 8 mg three times daily. Begin treatment before the allergy season (e.g., August 1st for ragweed) and continue until the allergen is no longer present (e.g., first frost in ragweed areas). Gradual dose increases help patients develop tolerance to sedative effects. 2. Cough Treatment: Administer 2 teaspoons (10 mL) of Codeprex™ (equivalent to codeine 40 mg and chlorpheniramine maleate 8 mg) orally every 12 hours, with a maximum of 4 teaspoons in 24 hours. 3. Off-Label Use: There is limited information regarding off-label uses of chlorpheniramine in adults. Pediatric Dosage and Indications: 1. FDA-Approved Dosage: Over-the-counter (OTC) cough and cold medications containing chlorpheniramine have been associated with reports of infant deaths. In January 2008, the FDA recommended against the use of such products in children under 2 years of age due to the risk of serious and life-threatening effects. Chlorpheniramine may cause excitability in children. The 8-hour and 12-hour allergy tablets are not recommended for children under 12 years, and the 4-hour tablets are not recommended for children under 6 years. Codeprex™ is not recommended for children under 6 years. For children aged 6 to 11 years, the dose is half the adult dose: 2 mg (half of a 4 mg tablet) every 4 to 6 hours, up to a maximum of 12 mg in 24 hours. The 8-hour and 12-hour tablets are not recommended for this age group. For allergic rhinitis, start with 2 mg and increase progressively to a maximum of 12 mg/day. For children 12 years or older, administer 2 teaspoons (10 mL) of Codeprex™ every 12 hours, with a maximum of 4 teaspoons in 24 hours. For children aged 6 to 12 years, administer 1 teaspoon (5 mL) every 12 hours, with a maximum of 2 teaspoons in 24 hours. 2. Off-Label Use: There is limited information regarding off-label uses of chlorpheniramine in pediatric patients. Contraindications: Chlorpheniramine is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to chlorpheniramine or dexchlorpheniramine. Warnings: Consult a doctor before use if you have breathing problems such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating due to an enlarged prostate. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking sedatives or tranquilizers. Drowsiness may occur; avoid alcohol and other sedatives as they may increase drowsiness. Exercise caution when driving or operating machinery. Excitability may occur, particularly in children. If pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. Adverse Reactions: There is limited information available regarding adverse reactions from clinical trials or post-marketing experience. Drug Interactions: Chlorpheniramine may interact with various medications, including but not limited to: amitriptyline, bupropion, fluoxetine, fentanyl, tramadol, and others. Consult a healthcare provider for a full list of potential interactions. Use in Specific Populations: Pregnancy: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of chlorpheniramine during pregnancy. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available. Nursing Mothers: No FDA guidance is available. Pediatric Use: No specific FDA guidance is available. Geriatric Use: No specific FDA guidance is available. Gender, Race, Renal, or Hepatic Impairment: No specific FDA guidance is available. Immunocompromised Patients: No specific FDA guidance is available. Administration and Monitoring: There is limited information regarding the administration and monitoring of chlorpheniramine. Overdosage: Limited information is available regarding chlorpheniramine overdose. In case of suspected overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Pharmacology: Limited information is available regarding the pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of chlorpheniramine. Patient Counseling Information: Take chlorpheniramine every 4 to 6 hours, not exceeding 6 doses in 24 hours. Adults and children 12 years and older should take 1 tablet. Children aged 6 to under 12 years should take half a tablet. Consult a doctor for children under 6 years. Alcohol Precautions: The interaction between alcohol and chlorpheniramine has not been established. Consult your doctor about the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication.
